chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-‘Ala’ ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man denies paternity of his child, although he had previously acknowledged it.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the child was from a free woman, he is whipped with the penalty of fifty lashes, which is the penalty for a slave; and if it was from a slave girl, there is nothing upon him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a man who denies paternity of a child he previously acknowledged?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the hadd punishment for a man acknowledging paternity yet later denying it, distinguishing between the status of the mother. If the mother is a free woman, the man receives fifty lashes, reflecting the hadd for a slave; if she is a slave girl, he incurs no penalty. This ruling highlights the nuanced application of penal codes in Shia jurisprudence based on the mother's social status.
